description:
Episode 49 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌧️
Titan, Saturn's largest moon: a thick orange atmosphere, methane rain, rivers and seas, the Huygens landing in 2005, and NASA's Dragonfly drone, planned to launch in 2028 and arrive in 2034.

#space #titan #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Titan is Saturn's biggest moon. It's larger than the planet Mercury.
segments.headline: Bigger than Mercury

segments.text: It's the only moon in the solar system with a thick atmosphere. A golden haze hides its surface.
segments.headline: A thick, hazy sky

segments.text: The air pressure on the ground is about one and a half times what you feel on Earth.
But it's freezing: about minus one hundred eighty degrees Celsius.
So cold that methane, a gas on Earth, falls as rain. It carves rivers, and fills lakes and seas.
segments.headline: Methane rain

segments.text: Titan and Earth are the only worlds we know with liquid lakes on the surface.
segments.headline: Lakes and seas

segments.text: In two thousand five, the European Huygens probe parachuted down and landed. It's still the farthest landing ever made.
segments.headline: Huygens landed, 2005

segments.text: Next, NASA's Dragonfly, a nuclear-powered drone, will fly from place to place studying Titan's chemistry.
segments.headline: Dragonfly drone

segments.text: It's planned to launch in twenty twenty-eight and arrive in twenty thirty-four.
Tomorrow, the most volcanic place in the solar system. Next stop: Io. Follow, so you don't miss episode fifty.
